answer: A nadir audit checks each lagoon circle of five identities that insure one another, each posting a 400,000 POA bond into a shared pool. When the audit traces any member to a second identity of the same operator, the fake loses its full reward of about 258,000 POA plus its bond, the other four forfeit theirs too, and the pool passes to honest peers. One fake therefore costs at least 658,000 POA, and five fakes cost 3,290,000 POA. The hollow promise of shared fate makes each circle police its own members first.
